newsitem.title: USA: Trunkline says most USG shut-in gas back.
newsitem.headline: Trunkline says most USG shut-in gas back.

text.p: Panenergy Corp unit Trunkline Gas said Tuesday that about 200 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of natural gas cut this week by producers ahead of Tropical Storm Josephine was restored this morning.
"About 200 million (cfd) was flowing this morning. The other 150 million (cfd) should be back on by tomorrow morning," a company spokesman said.
Producers this week cut about 350 mmcfd on the Trunkline system as they evacuated platforms in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico ahead of the storm.

Another Panenergy unit, Texas Eastern, said earlier that gas was trickling back on its system but about 300 mmcfd was still shut in. The company said it expected the majority of flows to be restored on Wednesday.

Josephine was downgraded overnight from a tropical storm, as it dissipated when it moved across Florida. At 1100 EDT, the storm was near Kinston, North Carolina, moving northeast at 40 mph, with winds of about 50 mph.
